messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

The raw report histories will be processed as follows: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff (knowledge_cutoff = 100). So we only consider reports received_time <= 100. In our reports, all reports have received_time from 3 to 96, all less than 100. So all are included.

Then choose the highest visible revision for each event_id. Since all revisions are 1 (and no alternate revisions exist), we keep each event as is.

Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. target_time = 100. So we keep all events with event_time <= 100. All events in reports have event_time up to 96. So all events are included.

Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock = 8. If multiple events have same event_time, we break ties by event_id order (presumably lexicographic). 

Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff, even if its event occurred earlier. Not relevant.

After reconstructing historical state: we need to compute: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after scenario; future_lost for scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time (earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand), or -1 if no future demand is unmet.

We need to process events in chronological order up to target_time (100). That yields stock_at_target (stock after processing up to time <= target_time). Also compute total historical_lost across those events (any unmet demand). Then after reconstructing the full historical state (i.e., after processing all events up to target_time, we have a stock at that point). Then we apply every event in future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock (the stock at time = after historical events, i.e., after 100). This is simulated to horizon_time = 130 (target horizon). Then after processing all future schedule events up to horizon_time (which includes all future events at times 103 to 130 inclusive), we have stock_at_horizon (stock after all events up to the horizon). Also compute future_lost (sum of unmet demand in these future events). Also compute first_future_stockout_time: earliest future event time where demand had unmet quantity (i.e., demand > stock). This is the first such event; if none, -1.

Now we must treat receipts and demands exactly: receipts increase stock, no constraints. Demands consume stock: quantity consumed = min(stock before demand, quantity). Unmet = quantity - min(stock, quantity) = max(0, quantity - stock). Unmet demand is "lost" (lost sales). So that counts toward lost. Also a stockout is when unmet > 0.
